title: Could you recommend the best AI for generating sprites—one that ensures the sprites remain stylistically consistent with each other for a game? Something along the lines of the aesthetic/art style seen in the work of "Nano Banana."

comments.author: KasperzackGames
comments.body:
For one character across many frames, what helped me most is generating all frames in a single image instead of one by one:

1. Ask for the whole sheet in one go: "a sprite sheet of \[character\], 12 frames in one image, 4 columns and 3 rows of equal square cells, the character centred on the same point in every cell, same size in every frame". Frames made in one image stay much closer to each other than separate generations.
2. Ask for a flat solid background like pure magenta #FF00FF. The grey checkerboard in your image is drawn in, not real transparency, so it's hard to cut out cleanly.
3. Once one sheet looks right, attach it as the reference for every other animation (walk, attack, hurt) and say "the same character in exactly the same style, size and colors as the attached sheet".
4. Clean the whole sheet at once: scale it down with nearest neighbour to your real sprite size and map every frame to one fixed palette (in Aseprite: load the palette, then Sprite > Color Mode > Indexed). One shared palette and grid is what stops the frames from flickering in color.
5. Slice it by the equal cells and play it in the engine before you generate more; regenerate a sheet with a frame that jumps rather than fixing it by hand.

I did this for an animated explosion with OpenAI's image model through Codex. I haven't tried Nano Banana for it, so I can't say how it compares.

comments.author: No-Dragonfruit-675
comments.body:
There's a few techniques that can help with this depending on what you're trying to do.  
  
**Character consistency: Use a character sheet as a reference anchor.** This helps lock in a character's appearance and style across subsequent generations.  
  
**Cross-character animation consistency: Animate a stand-in character first.** Generate an animation using a stand in, then use that animation as a reference to apply the same motion sequence to multiple characters.  


https://i.redd.it/y57cfp0gnm0i1.jpeg

  
  
**Color consistency: Redraw AI generated pixels using a limited color palette.** Stick to a fixed palette and a proper pixel grid to maintain consistent colors and pixel art aesthetics.

comments.author: Ill-Ant-9489
comments.body:
The one-sheet trick and a character anchor hold one character's frames together, but they drift once you have lots of different sprites, which sounds like your real problem. What holds a look across a whole set is a small style LoRA, feed it a dozen or two sprites that already match and any new subject comes out in that style. That plus the curation is what my app does (https://github.com/perfectgf/lora-dataset-studio), shameless plug.

For sprites the prep matters more than usual, consistent framing and sizes, no near duplicates, or it learns the mess. You can even seed the set with Nano Banana frames you like, then train so you are not API bound forever. How many sprites in that style do you have so far?
